cases.sentence: — Граф страдает и физически и нравственно, и, кажется, вы позаботились о том, чтобы причинить ему побольше ___.
cases.explain: «нравственных страданий» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “The count is suffering physically and mentally, and apparently you have done your best to increase his mental sufferings.”

cases.sentence: — М. Pitt comme traitre à la nation et au droit des gens est condamné à...[154] Питт, как изменник нации и ___, приговаривается к...
cases.explain: «народному праву» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “England is done for,” said he, scowling and pointing his finger at someone unseen. “Mr. Pitt, as a traitor to the nation and to the rights of man, is sentenced to …” But before Pierre—who at that moment imagined himself to be Napoleon in person and to have just effected the dangerous crossing of the Straits of Dover and captured London—could pronounce Pitt’s sentence, he saw a well-built and handsome young officer entering his room. Pierre paused. He had left Moscow when Borís was a boy of fourteen, and had quite forgotten him, but in his usual impulsive and hearty way he took Borís by the hand with a friendly smile.

cases.sentence: Его всё тревожат, — отвечал Пьер, стараясь вспомнить, кто этот ___.
cases.explain: «молодой человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, it seems he is ill. People are always disturbing him,” answered Pierre, trying to remember who this young man was.

cases.sentence: И Борис, видимо свалив с себя тяжелую обязанность, сам выйдя из ___ и поставив в него другого, сделался опять совершенно приятен.
cases.explain: «неловкого положения» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: And Borís, having apparently relieved himself of an onerous duty and extricated himself from an awkward situation and placed another in it, became quite pleasant again.

cases.explain: «удивительный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “No, but I say,” said Pierre, calming down, “you are a wonderful fellow! What you have just said is good, very good. Of course you don’t know me. We have not met for such a long time … not since we were children. You might think that I … I understand, quite understand. I could not have done it myself, I should not have had the courage, but it’s splendid. I am very glad to have made your acquaintance. It’s queer,” he added after a pause, “that you should have suspected me!” He began to laugh. “Well, what of it! I hope we’ll get better acquainted,” and he pressed Borís’ hand. “Do you know, I have not once been in to see the count. He has not sent for me. … I am sorry for him as a man, but what can one do?”

cases.sentence: По уходе его Пьер долго еще ходил по комнате, уже не пронзая невидимого врага шпагой, а улыбаясь при воспоминании об этом милом, умном и твердом ___.
cases.explain: «молодом человеке» — the prepositional is used only after a preposition, for location or topic.
cases.translation: A footman came in to summon Borís—the princess was going. Pierre, in order to make Borís’ better acquaintance, promised to come to dinner, and warmly pressing his hand looked affectionately over his spectacles into Borís’ eyes. After he had gone Pierre continued pacing up and down the room for a long time, no longer piercing an imaginary foe with his imaginary sword, but smiling at the remembrance of that pleasant, intelligent, and resolute young man.

cases.sentence: Как это бывает в первой молодости и особенно в ___, он почувствовал беспричинную нежность к этому молодому человеку и обещал себе непременно подружиться с ним.
cases.explain: «одиноком положении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: As often happens in early youth, especially to one who leads a lonely life, he felt an unaccountable tenderness for this young man and made up his mind that they would be friends.

cases.sentence: Как это бывает в первой молодости и особенно в одиноком положении, он почувствовал беспричинную нежность к этому ___ и обещал себе непременно подружиться с ним.
cases.explain: «молодому человеку» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: As often happens in early youth, especially to one who leads a lonely life, he felt an unaccountable tenderness for this young man and made up his mind that they would be friends.

cases.sentence: — Ах, он в ___, — сказала мать сыну, когда они опять садились в карету.
cases.explain: «ужасном положении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Oh, he is in a dreadful state,” said the mother to her son when they were in the carriage. “He hardly recognizes anybody.”

cases.explain: «недостаточная причина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Well, that is hardly a sufficient reason, Mamma …”
